questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Adjust your lane position to match changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quicker.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your lane position to match changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Adjust your lane position as needed, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle must be more visible than a car.
A motorcycle does not need to be as visible as a car.
Pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
Make eye contact with the other driver when passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle must be more visible than a car.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more important for motorcycles than cars. A motorcycle is smaller and can easily hide in a car's blind spot. Drivers may not see you even if they are looking.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a rider stay visible?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight at all times
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To stay visible, wear bright colors with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic moves.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to get through quickly.
Not weave between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between cars is dangerous. You may hit opening car doors or cars pulling into traffic. You won't have room to escape a hazard. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: To increase your visibility, you should:

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Stay visible by wearing bright colors and reflective materials, keeping your headlight on at all times, and changing your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep the motorcycle straight. Just before impact, roll off the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should NOT:

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, allow side vision, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight face shield causes fogging and blocks your vision.

questions.question: Usually, the best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to distance yourself from them.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest approach is to let the tailgater pass. Change lanes safely if you can. Speeding up may make the danger worse by encouraging them to follow faster.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged.
Release the front brake and re-apply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and re-apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake immediately. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
You stop sooner than expected.
A tire blows out.
It takes longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause your wheels to lose grip on the road. This can lead to a crash.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do with gears?

options.text: Shift gears while turning.
Shift gears before turning.
Change power suddenly while turning.
Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before turning.
questions.explanation: Shift to the correct gear before you enter a turn.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to during the day?

options.text: Keep a longer following distance at night.
Keep a shorter following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance all the time.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distance because there are fewer visual clues. Always use a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They happen in the dark.
They involve inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who do not have much experience.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection?

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers see you as early as possible.
Always ride in the left lane, away from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is more noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane that makes other drivers see you as soon as possible. For example, if there is a blind corner to your right, ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Is not allowed.
Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet or vest makes you visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: How should a rider position themselves to control a motorcycle best?

options.text: Sit with arms fully stretched out.
Use arms to hold up their body.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: What is true about riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It lets you use more of the road.
It should be avoided because you have fewer escape routes.
It makes it easier to communicate.
It makes it easier for other vehicles to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be avoided because you have fewer escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. It limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Keep a shorter following distance than when riding alone.
Ride faster than usual.
Brake later than you would when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight. Your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your following distance, and look for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: Tire inflation pressure.
Tire tread depth.
How reflective your tires are.
The condition of the tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of the tire sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: When securing a load, where should you place it?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and centered. High loads, like those on a sissy bar, raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and make it harder to balance. Distribute weight evenly on both sides of the bike.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Only a few minutes.
More than an hour.
It should be complicated.
You don't need to do it before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a quick inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. It takes just a few minutes and is very important for your safety.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, squeeze both brake levers at the same time.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: Less than half.
About 70 percent.
It should only be used on wet roads.
It should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing a brightly-colored helmet?

options.text: It may make it easier for others to see you.
It can be distracting.
It doesn't help visibility.
Bright colors are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may make it easier for others to see you.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects your head in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.
